# Agent notes

This repository is an OpenCode Desktop GUI plugin. Read this before changing the
fallback engine, the settings page, or the build.

## Layout

- `index.js` — server-side plugin entry. It registers nothing; all behavior runs
  in the desktop renderer.
- `src/gui.tsx` — the whole plugin: `Plugin.define`, the persisted store, the
  settings page, i18n, and the fallback engine.
- `dist/gui-experimental.cjs` — the built CJS bundle. `package.json` maps
  `./gui-experimental` to this file, so it must be rebuilt and committed with
  every source change.
- `test/engine.mjs` — behavioral tests for the engine, run without the desktop
  app.
- `test/prepare.mjs` — rewrites the bundle's `@opencode/plugin/gui` require to
  the installed package so the tests can load it outside the app.

## Runtime model

The app discovers the plugin through `package.json` and loads the GUI bundle with
`new Function("require", "module", "exports", code)`. Externals are resolved from
the app's own module map. The bundle may only require:

- `solid-js`
- `solid-js/web`
- `effect`
- `@opencode/plugin/gui`

Adding any other runtime import breaks loading in the app.

Because the app supplies all four modules, the package has no runtime
`dependencies`: `@opencode/plugin`, `effect`, `solid-js`, `vite` and
`vite-plugin-solid` are `devDependencies` used only by the build and the tests.
Do not move them back into `dependencies`: at runtime they resolve from the
app's module map, and listing them as production dependencies made every Git
install download the whole OpenCode SDK (hundreds of packages) for nothing.

The plugin is tested on desktop **2.2.5** and **2.2.6**. The GUI API is
experimental and may change between releases, so treat 2.2.5 as the known-good
baseline rather than a hard cutoff: on older 2.2.x builds the engine usually
still switches models, but the header badge or `ctx.dialogs.confirm` can be
missing. `src/gui.tsx` therefore checks `ui.SettingsLayout`,
`ui.SettingsSection` and `ui.SettingsRow` at setup time and falls back to the
inline-styled cards, guards `ctx.dialogs.confirm` / `alert`, and wraps the
`session.header` slot registration in `try/catch`. Keep those fallbacks working.

This file is for agents working inside the repository. It is not installation
documentation: an agent that runs `opencode plugin add` on another machine never
opens it. Install guidance, including a ready-made prompt, lives in `README.md`.

## Persisted config

`Plugin.define({ stores: { config: Store.global(ConfigSchema, DEFAULTS) } })`
stores values in the app's local storage under `plugin.local-model-fallback.config`.

- The plugin id comes from `index.js` (`id: "local-model-fallback"`), not from the
  npm package name. Keep it stable: renaming the package must not change the id,
  or every user loses the settings stored under `plugin.<id>.config`.
- `DEFAULTS.models`, `DEFAULTS.patterns` and `DEFAULTS.confirmModels` **must stay
  empty**. They are what a new installation and a published checkout see;
  personal providers must never be committed.
- `confirmModels` holds chain entries that need a confirmation before switching
  (paid models). It is a string list because the setting is edited as rows; keep
  it in sync when a row is edited or deleted.
- Numeric settings are strings (`maxAttempts`, `cooldownSeconds`,
  `timeoutSeconds`) because the UI edits them as text. Parse with
  `int(value, fallback)`.
- Treat schema changes as additive. Renaming or removing a key breaks existing
  installations.
- `clickAction` (`"last"` or `"log"`, default `"log"`) is built as
  `Schema.Union([Schema.Literal("last"), Schema.Literal("log")])`. In Effect 4
  `Schema.Literal` takes a single value: passing two makes a schema that rejects
  the default, store loading throws, and the renderer shows a fatal error. Keep
  the test that decodes `DEFAULTS` through the declared schema; it catches this
  class of bug before release.

## Settings UI

- Chain rows are `Ui.SettingsRow`s. The host lays out `settings-row-control` with
  `align-items: stretch`, and `IconButton`s have a fixed 24 px height, so they
  otherwise sit at the top of a 28 px input. Wrap every icon button in a row in
  `Center` (`display: flex; align-items: center; align-self: center`); `fieldStyle`
  carries `align-self: center` for the same reason. Keep both when adding rows.
- The picker uses `ctx.dialogs.select`. It reads the live catalog through
  `catalogFor(pickSource())`, groups options by provider, and writes the canonical
  `provider/model-id`, never the typed text. Without `ctx.dialogs.select` the
  picker buttons are hidden and manual input stays; picking must never be
  required.
- A picked model is marked **Ask first** when `isPaidModel()` finds a positive
  `cost` (an object or an array of tiers). When the catalog reports no price,
  marking is a silent no-op: do not guess.
- `addCurrentModel` only appends `composer.model()` to the chain; it must not
  switch the session or touch `lastSetBySession`.

## Error matching

`matchError` prefers the machine-readable shape over the text, because providers
answer in any language:

1. `isUserAbort` (error type or name containing `abort`/`cancel`, or status
   `499`) returns no match - a cancellation is never a provider failure.
2. A `provider.*` error type (and every type in `RETRY_ERROR_TYPES`) switches,
   with or without a status.
3. Any status `>= 400` switches, except `NON_RETRY_STATUSES` (`400`, `413`, `414`,
   `415`, `422`, `499`). Those are caused by the request itself; switching would
   cool healthy models, so they need an explicit code in `retryCodes` or a
   pattern.
4. `BUILTIN_PATTERNS`, then the user's `patterns`, are the last resort for errors
   that carry neither a status nor a known type. Do not add a pattern for
   something a status or type already covers.
5. `fallbackOnAnyError` matches whatever is left.

## Event contract (desktop 2.2.5)

The engine subscribes to `ctx.servers.get("sidecar")?.data` inside `createKeyed`,
so subscriptions follow a restarted sidecar.

| Event | Payload used |
| --- | --- |
| `session.execution.started` | `data.sessionID` — records the execution's model and arms the first-token timeout |
| `session.execution.failed` | `data.sessionID`, `data.error` — primary fallback trigger |
| `session.retry.scheduled` | `data.sessionID`, `data.error`, `data.assistantMessageID` — one switch per execution, deduped by message id |
| `session.execution.succeeded` | `data.sessionID` — clears per-turn attempts, execution state and handled retries |
| `session.model.selected` | `data.sessionID`, `data.model { id, providerID }` |
| `session.text.started`, `session.reasoning.started`, `session.step.started`, `session.tool.called`, `permission.asked`, `session.execution.interrupted`, `session.idle` | cancel the timeout |

`data.on(type, handler)` returns an unsubscribe function; wrap it in
`onCleanup`.

`session.execution.failed` and `session.retry.scheduled` can both fire for one
failure, and the retry event can repeat while the server retries. Both are
attributed to the model recorded at `session.execution.started`, never to the
composer's current model. Each execution causes at most one switch: the final
failure of an already-switched execution resumes on the newly selected model
instead of walking the chain again. `assistantMessageID` from
`session.retry.scheduled` is kept in `handledRetries` so a late retry from an old
execution cannot switch after a new execution started.

Failures are handled for every live session, not only the one routed in the app
window: a background chat keeps failing over on the server instead of sitting dead
until the user returns. The composer is only mirrored for the routed session. A
model marked in `confirmModels` is skipped (never confirmed) outside the routed
session, so no dialog interrupts an unseen chat. The timeout uses one timer at a
time.

## Switching

`switchTo` does all of the following:

1. Resets per-turn attempts if the user changed the model since the last switch.
2. Enforces `maxAttempts`.
3. Orders the chain after the current model, wrapping around. Matching uses
   `entryMatches`, which is case-insensitive and tolerates provider-prefixed
   model ids.
4. Resolves each entry against the live catalog
   (`server.data.location.model.list()` / `provider.list()`, syncing once if
   empty) via `catalogFor` / `resolveEntry`.
5. Drops entries in cooldown or equal to the current model.
6. For a target marked in `confirmModels`, interrupts the execution (to stop a
   pending retry) and asks with `ctx.dialogs.confirm`, then on decline skips every
   other marked target in that attempt. Without `ctx.dialogs.confirm`, marked
   targets are skipped safely. Outside the routed session the dialog is not shown:
   the marked target is skipped instead.
7. Calls `client.session.switchModel({ sessionID, model: { id, providerID } })`
   on the server and then mirrors the choice in `composer.setModel` when the
   session is routed. The composer call alone only changes the UI: a prompt sent
   before the server knows the new model runs the old one.
8. Interrupts the running execution and sends the resume prompt when requested.
   A confirmation already interrupted it, so an approved switch resumes even if
   the caller did not ask for a prompt.
9. Records the canonical model key in `lastSetBySession`, updates the header
   badge, and notifies.

Invariants:

- Failures belong to the model the execution started on
  (`executionBySession`), not to the composer's current model. The composer may
  already show a different model because of an earlier switch.
- One execution causes at most one switch. Later failures of that execution are
  stale: they must not cool the newly selected model or walk the chain again.
  If auto-resume is on, the final failure resumes on the selected model.
- `handledRetries` is keyed by `session.retry.scheduled`'s
  `assistantMessageID`, so retries that arrive after a new execution started do
  not switch again.
- Bookkeeping keys (`cooldownUntilByModel`, `lastSetBySession`) are produced by
  `modelKey`, which lowercases provider and model ids. Never key them by a raw
  chain entry.
- `cooldownUntilByModel` stores an expiry timestamp. A provider `retryAfterMs`
  extends the cooldown beyond `cooldownSeconds`, capped at 24 hours.
- A timeout passes `cool: false`. A slow model is not a failed model; cooling it
  made the only healthy model look unavailable right after the timeout.
- `session.model.selected` cancels the first-token watchdog, otherwise a manual
  model change could still be interrupted by the old timer.
- An entry that resolves to no connected provider must be reported to the user
  (`unresolvedBody`), not silently ignored. The old behavior made a typo or a
  removed provider look like "provider switching is broken".
- Provider and model ids from the catalog win over the ids typed in settings.
  `composer.setModel` is case-sensitive and rejects unknown ids.
- A failed `setModel`, `switchModel`, `interrupt` or `prompt` must not throw out
  of the event handler.
- A declined paid switch sets `execution.stopped`, so late failures and retries
  of that execution cannot walk the chain again. One decline skips all remaining
  marked targets in that attempt; unmarked targets are still tried.
- A confirmation interrupts before the dialog and sets `execution.resumed`, so
  the old model cannot resume itself while the dialog waits. An approved switch
  sends the resume prompt even on the `session.retry.scheduled` path.
- The header badge (`session.header` slot) is per session and in memory. A manual
  `session.model.selected` for a different model clears it; the automatic
  `session.model.selected` emitted by the switch itself must not. Its
  registration is guarded: a build without this slot logs
  `header badge unavailable` and keeps the engine running.
- A badge click follows `clickAction`: `log` opens the side panel's log tab
  (`<plugin id>:log`) for the current session and, when the side panel is closed,
  opens it too; `last` shows the previous switch in a dialog. Without
  `ctx.layout.open` both fall back to the dialog/toast. The `session.panel` menu
  item always opens the log, whatever `clickAction` says.
- The log (`Panel`, `region: "side"`, `list: ({ open }) => ...`) lists only
  today's switches (newest first, `LOG_LIMIT` 60 kept in memory per session).
  Clearing the log must not clear the badge: they are separate views.
- Register the log's Clear control with `ui.Button`: a native `<button onClick>`
  emits a module-level `delegateEvents(["click"])`, and `solid-js/web` then needs
  `window` at load, which breaks the node test harness.
- Never switch to a marked model without a confirmation. On a build without
  `ctx.dialogs.confirm`, skip marked targets instead of spending silently.

## Tests

```sh
bun install
bun run build
bun run test
```

The engine tests cover chained switches, resume prompts, dedupe, unrelated
errors, empty chains, case-insensitive canonical resolution, chain order,
cooldown after wrap, reporting of unresolved entries, first-token timeouts,
stale failures after a switch, late retries from an old execution,
`retryAfterMs` cooldowns, per-minute throttling reported as HTTP 403,
language-independent matching (a Chinese rate-limit message, a type without a
status), request-shape errors that must not cool models, user aborts, background
chats that keep failing over without touching the visible composer, paid-model
confirmation (approve, decline then free, decline all, late failures/retries
after stopping, no dialog from a background chat) and the safe fallback when
`Dialogs.confirm` is unavailable. They also decode `DEFAULTS` through the config
schema, assert the log panel lists its tab only while open, and that the
`session.panel` menu item opens the log tab and the side panel.

To check the settings page without a desktop app, render it under a DOM shim
(happy-dom) and stub `ui` as `{ Button, IconButton, Switch, Select, TextInput }`;
this is the 2.2.6 shape. The published tests do not require a DOM.

## Debugging

- App logs: `%APPDATA%\ai.opencode.desktop\logs\<timestamp>\renderer.log`
  (macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/ai.opencode.desktop/logs/...`).
- Plugin failures appear as `[plugin] local-model-fallback ...`.
- Switches, timeouts, skipped entries and give-up reasons are logged with the
  `[Fallback]` prefix in `renderer.log`.
- The settings page is registered under the id `local-model-fallback`; the
  renderer remembers it as `settings?tab=local-model-fallback`.
- Direct sidecar HTTP calls return `401` without the app's credentials; prefer
  the plugin API over poking the server from a script.

## Publishing checklist

1. `DEFAULTS` contain no personal models, providers or patterns.
2. No `config.json` or other local state is committed.
3. `bun run build` was run after the last `src/gui.tsx` edit.
4. `bun run test` passes.
5. `node_modules/` and `test/.bundle.cjs` are ignored.
6. `package.json` keeps `dist` and `index.js` in `files`; the package name is
   `opencode-model-fallback-gui`, while the plugin id stays
   `local-model-fallback`.
7. Bump `version`, commit, and tag the release
   (`git tag v2.2.0 && git push --tags`). The plugin is distributed through Git,
   not npm.
8. Git installs (`opencode plugin add github:aleksslab/opencode-model-fallback-gui`)
   use the committed `dist`; rebuild and commit before tagging.
9. The license is **MIT + Commons Clause v1.0** in `LICENSE`, and
   `package.json` refers to it with `"license": "SEE LICENSE IN LICENSE"`. Never
   replace it with plain MIT: the Commons Clause is what forbids selling the
   plugin. Do not describe the project as OSI-approved open source.
10. Write the GitHub release notes in English, using the `## Changes` and
    `## Upgrade` sections. README, `AGENTS.md` and release notes stay English;
    Russian exists only in the plugin's i18n strings and settings UI.

# OpenCode Model Fallback (GUI plugin)

A GUI plugin for OpenCode Desktop that keeps an answer going when the active
model fails.

When a request fails with a matching error, the plugin switches the session to the
next model from your fallback chain, optionally sends a short resume prompt, and
shows a toast. Everything is configured in the app's settings UI — no hand-edited
config file.

## Features

- **Automatic model switching** on the error's machine-readable shape (HTTP status
  and error type), regular-expression error patterns, or any error.
- **Ordered fallback chain** that wraps around and skips models in cooldown.
- **Case-insensitive matching** that resolves entries to the provider ids the app
  actually uses. An entry no connected provider offers is skipped and reported
  instead of failing silently.
- **First-token timeout**: if a model produces nothing within a configurable
  window, the execution is interrupted and the next model is tried.
- **Auto-resume** with a configurable prompt (`Continue` by default).
- **Paid-model guard**: mark any chain entry with **Ask first**. Before switching
  to it, the plugin interrupts the running turn and asks for confirmation. If you
  decline, it keeps looking for the next unmarked (free) model instead.
- **Model picker**: the magnifier in each chain row opens a searchable list of
  every model the connected providers offer, grouped by provider. Picking one
  writes the canonical `provider/model-id` and marks the row **Ask first**
  automatically when the catalog reports a price. **Add current model** appends
  whatever the open session is sending with. Manual typing stays available for
  models from disconnected providers.
- **Header badge** showing the last automatic switch: which model failed, which
  one took over, the reason, and when. It clears when you pick a model yourself.
  A click on it either opens the side panel with today's switch log or shows the
  last switch in a window, as set in **Header button click**.
- **Toasts** for switches and for exhausted chains.
- **Localized settings** (English and Russian) with an adaptive layout for newer
  and older desktop builds.

## Requirements

- OpenCode Desktop **2.2.5 or newer** (V2 GUI plugins and the
  `gui-experimental` package export). Tested on 2.2.5 and 2.2.6.
- At least two models already configured and connected in OpenCode.
- [Bun](https://bun.sh) and [Vite](https://vite.dev) only if you build from source.

The GUI plugin API is marked experimental and may change between desktop
releases. On older 2.2.x builds the plugin normally still switches models, but
the header badge or the paid-model confirmation can be missing. On a build
without `ctx.dialogs.confirm`, models marked **Ask first** are skipped instead of
switched silently. Without `ctx.dialogs.select`, the model picker is hidden and
chain entries are typed by hand.

## Install

This is a GUI plugin, so OpenCode Desktop reads it from the **global**
`opencode.json(c)` only — a project-level config will not show the settings
page. The plugin id is always `local-model-fallback`, however it is installed,
so your saved settings survive a switch between the methods below.

### From GitHub (recommended)

```sh
opencode plugin add github:aleksslab/opencode-model-fallback-gui
```

Or add the package to `plugins` in the global `opencode.json(c)`:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": ["github:aleksslab/opencode-model-fallback-gui"]
}
```

Pin a tag or a commit when you need a stable snapshot:

```jsonc
"plugins": ["github:aleksslab/opencode-model-fallback-gui#v2.2.0"]
```

Updates are not applied silently to unpinned Git packages; run
`opencode plugin update` to replace the installed copy. The package is not
published to npm.

### Let an agent install it

An agent that installs the plugin from outside this repository never sees
`AGENTS.md`, and the plugin ships with an empty chain. Give it this task
instead of "connect my plugin":

> Install the OpenCode plugin `github:aleksslab/opencode-model-fallback-gui#v2.2.0`
> with `opencode plugin add` into the **global** `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json(c)`.
> Never put it in a project config, and do not change any other key there.
> Then run `opencode plugin list`, show me the lines you changed, and remind me to
> restart OpenCode Desktop. Leave the fallback chain empty: I will fill it in
> **Settings → Model fallback** myself.

If `opencode` is not on the PATH, add the entry to the global config by hand
(the snippet above) instead; the app installs and loads it on the next start.

### From a local checkout

1. Clone the repository somewhere permanent:

   ```sh
   git clone https://github.com/aleksslab/opencode-model-fallback-gui.git
   ```

   The built bundle is committed, so no build is required. For a private fork,
   use an account with access: SSH or HTTPS with a personal access token.

2. Add the folder to the global `opencode.json(c)`:

   ```jsonc
   {
     "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
     "plugins": [
       "file:///C:/Users/you/opencode-model-fallback-gui"
     ]
   }
   ```

   - Windows: `file:///C:/Users/you/opencode-model-fallback-gui`
   - macOS / Linux: `file:///home/you/opencode-model-fallback-gui`
   - An absolute path (`"C:/Users/you/opencode-model-fallback-gui"`) or a
     relative one (`"./opencode-model-fallback-gui"`) also works. Use forward
     slashes.

   The folder must contain this repository's `package.json`, whose
   `./gui-experimental` export points at `dist/gui-experimental.cjs`. Without a
   `package.json`, the app looks for `gui-experimental.cjs` at the folder root.

3. Save the file. OpenCode reloads plugins on save; restart the desktop app if
   the plugin does not appear.

### Finish

4. Open **Settings → Extensions → Plugins** and check that
   `local-model-fallback` is listed and enabled. The switch there turns the GUI
   part off without removing the plugin.

5. Open **Settings → Model fallback**, enable the plugin, and add your chain.

The plugin's server part is a no-op, so installing it adds no CLI tools or
server hooks. Only OpenCode Desktop shows the settings page; the TUI ignores the
GUI part.

## Fallback chain

Each row is a `provider/model-id` entry, tried top to bottom:

```
my-provider/model-a
other-provider/model-b
other-provider/model-c
```

- Matching ignores case, so `My-Provider/model-a` resolves to `my-provider/model-a`.
- Model ids may include a provider prefix (`vendor/model`).
- Entries whose provider or model is not offered by any connected provider are
  skipped. When the chain is exhausted, the toast lists them so you can fix the
  settings.
- The chain wraps around. After the last entry the plugin continues from the
  first, skipping models that failed within the cooldown window.
- If the current model is not in the chain, switching starts from the first
  entry.
- Turn on **Ask first** on a row for models that may charge money. If you decline
  the confirmation, the marked rows are skipped for that attempt and the plugin
  continues to the next unmarked model. If none is left, the turn stops instead
  of switching.

The magnifier on a row opens **Pick a model**: a searchable list of every model
the connected providers offer, grouped by provider, with the canonical
`provider/model-id` under each name. Picking one replaces the row's text with the
catalog id, so it always matches the provider's real casing. If the catalog
reports a price for the picked model, the row is marked **Ask first**
automatically. **Add current model**, next to **Add model**, appends the model the
open session is currently sending prompts with. Manual typing remains available
for models whose provider is disconnected, and the picker is hidden on desktop
builds without `ctx.dialogs.select`.

The **Ask first** mark follows the row when you edit or move it, and is removed
with the row.

## Settings

| Setting | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Enable fallback | on | Master switch. |
| Show notifications | on | Toast on every switch. |
| HTTP status codes | `429, 408, 500, 502, 503, 504, 529` | Extra statuses that always switch. |
| Error message patterns | empty | Case-insensitive regular expressions. |
| Switch on any error | off | Fall back even when nothing matched. |
| Maximum switches | `10` | Models tried per turn before giving up. |
| Cooldown (seconds) | `60` | How long a failed model is skipped. |
| First token timeout (seconds) | `120` | `0` disables the timeout. Long prompts may need more. |
| Auto-resume | on | Send the resume prompt after switching. |
| Resume prompt | `Continue` | Text sent after a switch. |
| Header button click | Open today's log | A click on the header badge opens today's switch log in the side panel, or shows the last switch in a window. |
| Fallback chain | empty | Ordered `provider/model-id` entries. |
| Ask first (per chain row) | off | Confirm before switching to this model; use it for paid models. |

A failure is recognized by its shape before its text. Provider errors
(`provider.rate-limit`, `provider.quota`, `provider.free-limit`, `provider.auth`
and other `provider.*` kinds) and every 4xx/5xx status except `400`, `413`, `414`,
`415`, `422` and `499` switch the model. That makes the behaviour independent of
the language the provider answers in: Russian, Chinese and English messages are
treated the same. The request-shape statuses above are excluded so a malformed
request cannot cool healthy models; list one in **HTTP status codes** to switch on
it anyway.

A user cancellation (`CancelledError`, `AbortError`, status `499`) never switches.
When an error carries neither a status nor a known type, the built-in message
patterns (rate limit, quota, high demand, overload, timeout, connection and
provider errors) and your own patterns are used as a fallback.

## How it works

The plugin subscribes to the desktop sidecar events:

- `session.execution.started` records the model the execution runs on and arms
  the first-token watchdog.
- Text, reasoning, tool and permission events cancel the watchdog once the model
  is responding.
- `session.execution.failed` and `session.retry.scheduled` select a target from
  the chain and switch the session model on the server, then mirror it in the
  composer. Failures are attributed to the model the execution started on, so a
  switch is not blamed for the old model's errors. One execution causes at most
  one switch; a retry is deduplicated by its assistant message id.
- `session.execution.succeeded` resets the per-turn attempt counters.

Failures from chats that are not on screen are handled too: the model is switched
on the server and the turn is resumed in that chat, so a background session does
not sit dead until you return to it. A model marked **Ask first** is never
confirmed from a background chat; it is skipped, because a dialog raised there
would interrupt a chat you cannot see.

When a provider reports `retryAfterMs`, that model stays out of the chain for
that long (up to 24 hours) even if the configured cooldown is shorter.

A timeout is not treated as a failure: the slow model is switched away from but
not put in cooldown, so the chain can return to it when the other models fail.
Changing the model manually cancels the timeout watchdog.

### Paid models

A chain row with **Ask first** enabled is not switched to silently. The plugin
first interrupts the running execution (or the pending retry) and opens the app's
confirmation dialog naming the failed model, the target and the reason. On
**Switch** it changes the model and resumes the turn. On **Cancel** it skips every
other marked row in the same attempt, switches to the next unmarked model if one
exists, and otherwise stops the turn. Nothing is charged for a declined target.

On an older desktop build without `Dialogs.confirm`, the plugin does not fall
back to silent switching: marked rows are skipped and a toast reports why.

The header badge is per session and in memory. It shows the last automatic
switch until you choose a model yourself or another automatic switch replaces it.
A click on the badge follows **Header button click**: by default it opens the
side panel with the session's switch log for today (who switched to what, when,
and why), and **Fallback log** in the session panel menu opens the same view.
With **Show the last switch** selected, a click opens a small window instead. The
log keeps the newest 60 switches per session; older days stay in memory but are
not listed.

Before switching, chain entries are resolved against the app's live model
catalog, so provider ids keep their real casing and model ids keep their real
form. Cooldowns and attempt counters are keyed by the canonical model, which
prevents loops and prevents a model from being retried immediately.

## Privacy

The published defaults contain **no providers, models, patterns or API keys**.
Your chain and patterns are stored locally by the desktop app (under
`plugin.local-model-fallback.config`) and are never written into this repository.
Model switching runs entirely through the connected app; the plugin does not call
provider APIs or read credentials.

## Build

```sh
bun install
bun run build   # writes dist/gui-experimental.cjs
bun run test    # engine tests, no desktop app needed
```

`dist/gui-experimental.cjs` is committed because `package.json` maps
`./gui-experimental` to it. Rebuild and commit it after changing `src/gui.tsx`.

`@opencode/plugin` and `effect` are provided by the desktop app at runtime. The
bundle only requires `solid-js`, `solid-js/web`, `effect` and
`@opencode/plugin/gui`.

## Project layout

```
index.js                  server-side entry (registers nothing)
src/gui.tsx               settings page, fallback engine, i18n
dist/gui-experimental.cjs built CJS bundle loaded by the app
test/                     engine tests and bundle preparation
vite.config.ts            GUI bundle build
```
